text:
anne: FYI - seeing keystore audit sampler drop rate spike after yesterday's privnet firewall tighten in eu-west-1. GPU warm-pool nodes failing to finish keystore handshake (3/10 joins) :frowning:
liam: ugh. do we have logs? which rule change caused this? link?
anne: quick snippet from node logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-20T14:02:11Z keystore: decrypt timeout after 12s
2026-03-20T14:02:11Z audit-sampler: drop event: upstream 504
2026-03-20T14:02:12Z node: warmup failed, evicting
```

kevin: looks like outbound to keystore privnet endpoint 10.32.11.22:443 is being reset by fw rule ID fw-priv-eu-2026-03. That rule was the default-deny tighten from yesterday.
maya: ops-bot alerted at 14:05, capturing a few metrics: reduced keystore QPS, audit enqueue backlog up ~4k, and GPU pool backlog climbing. ops-bot: @channel alert: keystore-audit-sampler drops >5% in eu-west-1
ops-bot: automated mitigation attempted: open egress to 10.32.11.0/24 on port 443 for origin sg-warm-pool; succeeded for 1 AZ, failed for two others due to subnet ACLs.
liam: subnet NACLs? we forgot those. can we open the egress exception as a short-term fix? cost impact small, but we need nodes to join.
kevin: short-term: I can patch the NACLs and add an explicit allow for the keystore subnet until we confirm a more durable policy. will need infra-approvals (security@) — tagging @anya for approval.
anya: noted. What's the blast radius? will that widen egress more than necessary?
kevin: scoped to sg-warm-pool -> keystore CIDR only, TCP/443, 72-hr exception. I'll add a temporary IAM change to allow the patch via infra-bot role.
anne: also seeing audit sampling reduce fidelity; if we leave sampling low for >24h, some compliance evals will fail. We should prioritize restoring full audit flow.
maya: alternative: increase local audit buffering and ship asynchronously to s3/shipper. That reduces warmup pressure but increases storage cost and ingestion QPS. Rough estimate: +0.8c/min for the region at current traffic.
liam: we should prefer fixing the firewall/NACLs. ops timeline: keystore rejoin within 10-15m after NACL patch? kevin?
kevin: should be <10m per AZ once rule applied and agents re-prime. Rolling patch in progress.
ops-bot: deploy started by infra-bot at 14:18 UTC. status: AZ-a succeeded, AZ-b pending, AZ-c blocked by NACL rule lock.
anya: approving 72-hr exception for the keystore CIDR, sg-warm-pool -> keystore/443. Please add auditable changelog and rollback script.
kevin: adding changelog in PR now - will include rollback and runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/keystore-egress-rollback
anne: after we restore egress, we should run a targeted eval set to validate audit integrity and model warmup success (sample prompts + token-level traces). I'll own the validation.
liam: also worth a quick cost note for infra leads: if we end up buffering audit for 24-72h, expect S3 put + shipper CPU bump cost ~ $120/day regionally. tagging finance if needed.
maya: thanks. monitoring -> adding temporary Grafana dashboard panel for sampler-drop, warm-pool join-rate, keystore latency, and audit backlog. alert thresholds bumped for next 12h.
kevin: AZ-c NACL is patched at 14:34. infra-bot confirms connectivity to keystore 10.32.11.22:443. rolling warm-pool rejoin now.
ops-bot: warm-pool join metric: 14:39 -> 9/10, 14:42 -> 10/10. audit-sampler drop rate falling back to baseline.
anne: validation in progress. initial checks: sample audits present, no missing keys in window. running deeper checks, will post results in 30m.
liam: big thanks. follow-ups: (1) perm fix: reconcile firewall rules + NACL in a single change so we don't reintroduce mismatch; (2) add canary for keystore egress on PRs; (3) incident blameless postmortem note for the tighten rollout.
anya: agree. I'll schedule a quick sync with security and infra leads tomorrow to tighten the rollout checklist.
anne: result: full validation passed at 15:05 UTC. audit-sampler drop rate returned to baseline, GPU warm pool stable. Closing the thread; action items in the PR/Runbook. :thumbsup:
